texts.title: Collecting rainwater in a water butt

paragraphs.text: A water butt is a large container that collects rainwater from the roof of a house or shed. A pipe called a downpipe carries water from the gutter to the ground, and a diverter fitted to this pipe sends some of the water into the butt.
The butt should have a lid to keep out leaves and insects and to stop children or animals falling in. Near the bottom is a tap, which is easier to use if the butt stands on a raised base.
When the butt is full, the diverter automatically sends extra water back down the downpipe, so the container does not overflow.
Rainwater is good for plants because it contains no chlorine, and using it reduces the amount of tap water a household needs in summer.
Most garden centres sell water butt kits that include the container, the lid, the tap and a diverter that fits standard downpipes.
